public_mechanism.authoritative_source: University of Wisconsin CS537 xv6 scheduler project by Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau
source_supported_core: jobs begin in a high-priority queue
when a job uses its time slice at the high-priority queue it is moved to a lower-priority queue
the mechanism uses observed slice consumption as feedback for subsequent scheduling priority
public_mechanism.adaptation: Use finite role-local queue levels and durable checkpoints. A full nonterminal Chat work slice causes one deterministic requeue to a lower immediate entitlement; no OS process scheduler or external executor is required.

fixed_trace_result.observed: E consumed the full H slice and remained nonterminal
effects: O remains H and becomes next eligible

scope_limit: Constructed two-item, three-level role-local scheduling trace only. This does not establish optimal queue parameters, runtime prediction accuracy, or equivalence to an operating-system MLFQ implementation.
